chunks: Muhammad ibn Qays narrated from Abu Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:
Amir al-Muʾminin عليه السلام ruled concerning the eye of a horse that was gouged out that the compensation is one quarter of its price on the day the eye was gouged out.

key_terms.بِرُبُعِ ثَمَنِهِ: one quarter of its price or market value
key_terms.عَيْنِ فَرَسٍ: the eye of a horse, the injured body part and animal under discussion
key_terms.يَوْمَ فُقِئَتِ الْعَيْنُ: the day on which the injury occurred, the time of valuation

ai.seo_question: What is the compensation if a horse’s eye is gouged out in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith records a legal ruling from Amir al-Muʾminin عليه السلام concerning compensation for injury to an animal. It establishes that if a horse’s eye is gouged out, the liability is assessed as one quarter of the horse’s value on the day the injury occurred.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5398 - Muhammad ibn Qays narrated from Abu Jafar Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) who said:
"The Commander of the Faithful (as) ruled that if the eye of a horse is gouged out, the compensation is a quarter of its value on the day its eye was gouged out."
